plan: With a private value of $35, my optimal strategy is to bid strategically. Since this is a single round with no repeated interactions, I want to bid just above the expected third-highest bid. Assuming rational bidders and values drawn uniformly between $0-$49, I'll aim to bid around $30-$35 to maximize potential profit. This gives me a good chance of winning while minimizing overpayment risk.

My private value is $32. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid close to my true value. Since the winner pays the third-highest bid, I want to bid high enough to likely win, but not so high that I risk negative earnings. I'll bid slightly above my value at $35 to increase my chances of winning while maintaining potential profit margin.

With a high private value of $48, I want to win the auction but minimize my payment. Since values are randomly drawn, rational opponents will also bid strategically. I'll bid slightly below my true value to maximize potential profit. A bid around $45-47 balances winning likelihood with payment minimization. This approach leaves room to potentially win while protecting against overpaying relative to my true value.
